Triage: `packages/plugin-detail/src/RelatedList.tsx` ⇒ **`domain:ui`**; **type `Bug`, `priority:p2`, `security`, `pm:queue`.**

## ⭐ A control that inverts under full application

Redacting **every** authored column hands `RelatedList` an empty array, and `effectiveColumns` reads an empty array as **"no columns were authored"** ⇒ it falls through to heuristic auto-derivation, where the block's `redactFields` list **is not in scope at all**.

⇒ **Redacting more produces less redaction.** ⛔ The single most counterintuitive failure a control can have: the author applies it maximally and it stops applying.

## Why p2 and not p1 — stated so the grade is checkable

⭐ **The real permission boundary holds.** The auto-derived path still runs `filterFK`, `pruneEmpty` and **`filterFLS`** — so `enforceFieldSecurity` is re-applied. What is lost is the **block-level `redactFields`**, an authoring preference layered on top.

⇒ ⛔ Not an FLS bypass, which is why it sits below its neighbour **#9054** (p1, where an unresolvable entry escapes `enforceFieldSecurity` itself). ⚠️ But it is `security`-labelled and real: an author who explicitly hid a field sees it displayed, silently, and has no signal that their configuration was discarded.

⚠️ **Independent of objectui#8793** — the filer measured this while sizing that card's blast radius and states plainly that #8793 ⛔ neither causes nor fixes it, and that this is reachable **today with entirely spec-canonical authoring**. ⛔ Do not close it when #8793 lands.

**Claim:** `domain:ui @ objectui` execution seat · dispatching now · batch 3

## ZONE 1 — rulings (binding)

**① The A/B fork in the card is ruled B, and the floor is what selects it — not a preference.**

The card offers two readings and explicitly declines to rule ("not a ruling"). Triage graded the card but did not rule it either. This seat rules it, on this reasoning, which is stated so it can be overturned:

- **B restores an invariant.** `redactFields` is a block-level policy deciding which columns are shown. There are two paths that decide columns — the authored one and the derived one — and the policy reaches exactly one. That is a scope defect: the policy was never ruled to stop at the authored path, it just never got there. Closing it is 恢复不变量, and it changes no user-visible outcome in any case that is not currently leaking.
- **A adds a rendered state that does not exist today.** "The author authored columns and security removed all of them" would become a new distinct outcome with its own empty/denied presentation. That is a **feature addition**, and feature additions are manual floor. This seat cannot author it.

⇒ Implement **B**. ⛔ Do **not** implement A, and do not add a denied/empty state. If B turns out to be unimplementable without answering A's question, **stop and report** — do not decide it.

**② The security half is determined; the presentation half is not.** Your mandate is: redaction must reach every path that decides columns. Your mandate is **not** to decide what an emptied-by-security list should look like.

**③ ⛔ Do not close or touch objectui#8793.** The card and triage both say this defect is independent of it — reachable today with spec-canonical authoring, and #8793 neither causes nor fixes it. Triage's ⛔ is explicit: *do not close it when #8793 lands*.

## ZONE 2 — PM assumptions to falsify (measure these, do not inherit them)

**⭐ A. Triage's p2 grade rests on one unverified measurement. Verify it FIRST.** Triage states the derived path *"still runs `filterFK`, `pruneEmpty` and `filterFLS` — so `enforceFieldSecurity` is re-applied,"* and that is the whole reason this is p2 and not p1, **and** the whole reason the fix is "push redaction down" rather than "push security down."

Measure it against the code. If `filterFLS` does **not** in fact re-apply on the derived path, then this is an FLS bypass, the grade is wrong, the shape of the fix is wrong, and you should **stop and report** rather than proceed on a false premise. A card whose priority and remedy both hang on one sentence deserves that sentence measured. (This seat has already spent one full dispatch on a triage measurement it re-published without re-deriving — objectui#8564. Not again.)

**B. "`redactFields` is not in scope there at all."** Confirm by reading, not by assuming. Establish where the list lives, where it dies, and whether anything else block-level dies at the same seam — if `redactFields` is one of several block-level policies that fail to reach `RelatedList`, say so; fix only redaction, and file the rest.

**C. The reproduction.** The card measures `[ 'Fix the pump', '90000' ]` from real DOM cells with `columns: [{ field: 'salary' }]` + `redactFields: ['salary']`. Reproduce it on an unfixed tree before you change anything, so your pin has a lit positive control. If it does not reproduce, that is a finding — report it.

**D. Does B widen a public surface?** Pushing a block-level list down to `RelatedList` may mean a new prop. If `RelatedList` (or its props type) is exported from the package's public entry, that is a **surface widening ⇒ `Clause-②: yes`**. Determine it by reading the barrel, and declare accordingly — do not guess in either direction.

**E. The partial case.** The card measures redacting *every* authored column. Also measure redacting *some* — the array is non-empty, the authored path is taken, and redaction presumably works. Confirm the fix does not disturb it. That is your control against "the fix now hides things it shouldn't."

## ZONE 3 — suggested route (not binding)

Reproduce → verify ZONE 2 A → thread the block's redaction policy to the path that derives columns so both paths are filtered by one policy → pin the maximal case, the partial case, and a no-redaction control → ablate with the direction predicted in advance.

## Hot file ⚠️ — an open PR is already sitting on this seam

`packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-related-list.tsx` currently has an open, **HELD** draft PR against it: objectui#9058 (card objectui#8793), which flips one filter's fail-open default to fail-closed. It is held **in draft on purpose, waiting on this card** — its landing note recommends exactly this ordering, because fail-closing that filter produces *more* emptied arrays and therefore *more* traffic into the hole you are closing.

⇒ You may edit that file. ⛔ You must **not** adopt, revert, or re-implement #9058's one-line change (`return n ? allowed.has(n) : false`) — it is another card's diff and its landing call is not yours. Work as if that line still reads `: true`, because on `main` it does. #9058 rebases onto you after you land.

## Carrier lifecycle (⭐ corrected — an earlier brief from this seat had this backwards)

If your claim declares `Clause-②: yes`, **you hang `needs:contract-review` on BOTH carriers** (this card and your PR) in the same pass that opens the PR — `os-dev.md:288`. Add it **additively**: a `POST` to `.../issues/N/labels` adds one label; an issue-update call **replaces the whole set** and will silently drop `pm:dispatched`, `priority:p2`, `security` and `domain:ui`. Then report `check-clause2-carriers --pair <PR>` in your return.

⛔ Do **not** clear the label yourself, and do not treat it as a blocker. **This seat is the reviewer** (`contract-review.md:27`) and clears both carriers on a PASS before landing (`:38`, `:42`). Earlier briefs from this seat told devs not to hang it and called the reviewer absent; that was wrong and is retracted in full on objectui#8568.

## Commit trailers

End commits with exactly:

```
Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01MPaVWWMuWeT5LgB1qoXjVB
```

⛔ No model identifier in any commit message, PR title or body, code comment, or anything else pushed to the repository.

`packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx` exports BOTH the component and its props
type — `export { DetailView, DetailSection, DetailTabs, RelatedList }` and
`export type { RelatedListProps } from './RelatedList'` — and the package's only
`exports` entry is `.` onto `dist/index.d.ts`. Implementing ruling B threads the
block's redaction list down as a new optional `RelatedList` prop, so it lands on
a published surface ⇒ clause ② holds.

Nothing was added to the block's registered `inputs`: `redactFields` is a
renderer-only key today (it is on neither `RecordRelatedListProps` in
`@objectstack/spec` nor this block's `inputs`), and declaring it would make it an
authoring surface — a call this seat does not own.

`needs:contract-review` hung additively on BOTH carriers in the same pass that
opened the PR (`POST .../issues/N/labels`, one label, existing set untouched),
and read back on both: card #9053 now carries
`bug, domain:ui, needs:contract-review, pm:dispatched, priority:p2, security`
(all five originals intact), PR #9090 carries `needs:contract-review, plugin, tests`.
⛔ Not cleared by this seat — the dispatching seat is the reviewer and clears both
carriers on a PASS.
